summary: I have to correct myself. Remember the 29,000 jobs print I wrote about? It has been revised to 60,000, and August and September together were revised up by 84,000. Then October came in at 165,000 against 65,000 expected, and unemployment fell to 4.1%. The labour market was never as weak as the first print said. First prints lie, revisions tell the truth. CPI on Tuesday: headline +0.4% on the month, core +0.3%, both above expectations. Recall: there is no year over year rate this time. BLS could not publish one, because last year's government shutdown wiped out the October 2025 data it would be measured against. So the site still shows September's 3.7%. Sometimes the number just doesn't exist. The market's answer was fast. The 2 year jumped 18bp in a session to *4.75%* and the 10 year went back through 5%. What does this even mean? For two months the long end moved on risk, not inflation, and I kept saying so. This week it flipped. The front end led, and the front end is pure Fed expectations. So this time it really is an inflation trade. Mixing this all in a pot: a strong jobs market, sticky monthly inflation, oil at a ten week low, and a Fed that held in October with two members voting to hike. December is live.
_fedPath_note: Every FOMC decision since the last hike, oldest first: the date, the upper bound of the target range after it, and hike / cut / hold. Drawn as the staircase under the Fed and listed in its card. Add a row after each meeting.

news.what: October CPI: headline +0.4% MoM and core +0.3%, both above expectations. BLS published no year over year rate, because last year's shutdown wiped out the October 2025 data.
2 year jumped 18bp in a session and the 10 year went back through 5%, as the market priced more hikes.
Payrolls +165,000 in October against 65,000 expected. August and September revised up by a combined 84,000. Unemployment fell to 4.1%.
Oil hit a 10 week low. Brent is down 13% on the month as peace talks drag on.
Democrats swept Congress in the midterms.
Q3 GDP came in at 3.4% annualised, up from 2.2% in Q2.
Fed held at 3.75-4.00%. Two policymakers voted to hike.

_oil_note: Optional daily override. Set asOf to the date you read them and fill wti/brent. Used only while newer than FRED's print - if you stop updating, it falls back to FRED automatically rather than showing an ever-staler number.

notes.2Y: Up 18bp in a session on the CPI

_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only. Put alert on whatever the day's story is: it turns the figure rust and is the only thing telling a first-time visitor where to look. strain is the quieter version: a smaller crack on the summit, number stays in ink. track is [open, low, now] for one tenor's day, drawn as a path under the summit; use it only when the path matters more than the close, and leave it out otherwise.
